en.headline: Forty percent of pedestrian crossings now have new audible devices
en.dek: The Transport Department has upgraded more than 800 junctions and expects to finish the citywide programme of about 2,000 sites by the end of 2027.
body: More than 800 pedestrian crossings across Hong Kong, about 40 percent of the total, have been fitted with new-generation electronic audible traffic signals, the Transport Department said.

The department began the district-by-district replacement in April 2025. Chief Engineer for Traffic Control Gordon Kwok Ka-chun said progress was on track and the full set of roughly 2,000 junctions should be completed by the end of 2027. Priority has been given to areas with higher numbers of visually impaired pedestrians, such as Sham Shui Po and Kwun Tong.

The upgraded yellow boxes retain sound and vibration cues and add five features: a light to help low-vision users locate the post, a tactile map of the crossing layout, voice prompts that announce nearby street names in Cantonese, Putonghua and English, contactless push-button sensors, and a quieter night-time mode that can be raised temporarily by remote control or the HKeMobility app.

About 15,000 dedicated remote controls have been distributed free through organisations for the visually impaired. Users and advocates have welcomed the quieter night setting combined with on-demand volume boost as a practical compromise for both residents and pedestrians.

zh.headline: 全港四成行人過路處已換新一代發聲裝置
zh.dek: 運輸署稱進度理想，預期2027年底前完成約2,000個路口更換，優先深水埗及觀塘。
body: 運輸署表示，截至今年8月已完成超過800個行人過路處的新一代電子行人過路發聲裝置更換工程，相當於全港約四成。
署方自2025年4月起分區逐步更換。運輸署總工程師（交通控制）郭家駿指進度理想，預期2027年年底前可完成全港約2,000個路口的目標。署方優先處理視障人士活動較多的地區，例如深水埗及觀塘。
新裝置保留聲響及震動提示，並新增五項功能：發光組件協助弱視人士定位、摸讀地圖顯示過路佈局、語音位置提示以粵語、普通話及英語讀出附近街道名稱、非接觸式按鍵，以及夜間減音模式。視障人士可用專屬遙控器或「香港出行易」應用程式短暫提高音量。
政府已透過視障機構派發約15,000個專屬遙控器。用家及倡議者歡迎夜間減音與按需提高音量的安排，認為同時照顧居民及行人需要。
